finding.claim: Expired-token acceptance via the verification cache. cacheSet only records the token's exp/nbf into the cache entry when the payload has a numeric iat. A validly signed token with exp but no iat is cached with an expiry of now + cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) and is served from the cache after its own exp has passed, because the cache-hit path never re-runs claim validation.
finding.source: A signed JWT with a numeric `exp` and no `iat` claim, for example from an issuer or signer using noTimestamp. The attacker is a holder of such a token (or a replayer of a captured one), presented to a verifier created with `cache` enabled.
finding.sink: Cache-hit return in verify() (src/verifier.js:377), which returns the cached payload as valid without checking exp.

trace.note: First verification succeeds (token not yet expired) and calls cacheSet(cacheContext, payload).
hasIat is false because payload.iat is not a number.
The block that sets cacheValue[1] (nbf) and cacheValue[2] (exp) sits inside `if (hasIat)`, so for a token with no iat it is skipped and both stay 0.
cacheValue[2] === 0, so it is set to maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL (default 600000 ms), ignoring the token's real exp.

Later calls with the same token find the entry. With min === 0 and now <= max the cache hit is accepted and the cached payload is returned (line 377). decode and verifyToken, which check exp, are skipped.

finding.guards_checked: cacheTTL caps the entry lifetime (default 10 minutes), so the extra validity window is at most cacheTTL after the first verification. Exp is enforced on the uncached path by the validators in verifyToken (src/verifier.js:304-323). When iat is present, the exp-aware cache expiry at lines 123-129 applies. Nothing in the no-iat case bounds the cache entry to exp. The decoder and key checks run only on a cache miss. The cache is on only when the `cache` option is set; `createCache` returns null otherwise.
